name: Relative Hitting Size
definition: The **Relative Hitting Size** is $\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\mathrm{HT}(\{h'\mathbin{\triangle}h:h'\in\mathcal{H}\})$; equivalently, it is the maximum teaching-set size.
graph_summary: The worst hitting size after translating the class by one of its concepts.

monotonic.proof: Relative hitting size equals maximum teaching-set size (teaching dimension), which is monotonic under subfamilies by restricting each target's teaching set.

c_monotonic.proof: This is equal to maximum teaching-set size; the latter is c-monotonic by restricting each teaching set to the unfixed coordinates.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: Relative hitting size equals teaching dimension. The class $\{001,010,100\}$ has value 1, while projection away the first coordinate gives $\{00,01,10\}$, whose value is 2 by the teaching-dimension projection counterexample.
